## 1) Chart type
- **Top panel:** A **categorical timeline dot plot** (scatter/dot plot arranged by category), showing presidents’ first election year against their highest previous position.
- **Bottom panel:** A **table with pictorial marks** (candidate headshots) plus numeric/text columns.

## 2) Layout techniques
- The visualization uses **two vertically stacked panels**.
- **Top panel:** Categories are arranged as horizontal rows; dots are positioned along a shared time axis. This is a **small-multiple-by-row / categorical layout**, not stacked.
- **Bottom panel:** A **tabular layout** with rows for position categories and columns for candidate icons, counts, and most recent election year.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Highest previous position of each U.S. president | Categorical/nominal | Position on y-axis / row placement in top panel |
| Date/year of first election | Temporal | Position on x-axis in top panel |
| Individual president identity (for selected labeled points) | Categorical/nominal | Text labels next to highlighted dots |
| President occurrence / one president per mark | Categorical/nominal (entity) | Individual dot marks in top panel |
| 2020 candidates | Categorical/nominal | Headshot images/icons in the “2020 candidates” column of the table |
| Number elected president | Quantitative | Numeric text in the “No. elected president” column |
| Most recently elected (year or “never”) | Temporal (year) / categorical for “never” | Text in the “Most recently elected” column |
| Highest previous position (table rows) | Categorical/nominal | Row labels in bottom table |

## 1) Chart type
- **Top panel:** A **categorical timeline dot plot** (scatter/dot plot arranged by category), showing presidents’ first election year against their highest previous position.
- **Bottom panel:** A **table with pictorial marks** (candidate headshots) plus numeric/text columns.

## 2) Layout techniques
- The visualization uses **two vertically stacked panels**.
- **Top panel:** Categories are arranged as horizontal rows; dots are positioned along a shared time axis. This is a **small-multiple-by-row / categorical layout**, not stacked.
- **Bottom panel:** A **tabular layout** with rows for position categories and columns for candidate icons, counts, and most recent election year.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Highest previous position of each U.S. president | Categorical/nominal | Position on y-axis / row placement in top panel |
| Date/year of first election | Temporal | Position on x-axis in top panel |
| Individual president identity (for selected labeled points) | Categorical/nominal | Text labels next to highlighted dots |
| President occurrence / one president per mark | Categorical/nominal (entity) | Individual dot marks in top panel |
| 2020 candidates | Categorical/nominal | Headshot images/icons in the “2020 candidates” column of the table |
| Number elected president | Quantitative | Numeric text in the “No. elected president” column |
| Most recently elected (year or “never”) | Temporal (year) / categorical for “never” | Text in the “Most recently elected” column |
| Highest previous position (table rows) | Categorical/nominal | Row labels in bottom table |

- **Top panel:** A **categorical timeline dot plot** (scatter/dot plot arranged by category), showing presidents’ first election year against their highest previous position.
- **Bottom panel:** A **table with pictorial marks** (candidate headshots) plus numeric/text columns.

## 2) Layout techniques
- The visualization uses **two vertically stacked panels**.
- **Top panel:** Categories are arranged as horizontal rows; dots are positioned along a shared time axis. This is a **small-multiple-by-row / categorical layout**, not stacked.
- **Bottom panel:** A **tabular layout** with rows for position categories and columns for candidate icons, counts, and most recent election year.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Highest previous position of each U.S. president | Categorical/nominal | Position on y-axis / row placement in top panel |
| Date/year of first election | Temporal | Position on x-axis in top panel |
| Individual president identity (for selected labeled points) | Categorical/nominal | Text labels next to highlighted dots |
| President occurrence / one president per mark | Categorical/nominal (entity) | Individual dot marks in top panel |
| 2020 candidates | Categorical/nominal | Headshot images/icons in the “2020 candidates” column of the table |
| Number elected president | Quantitative | Numeric text in the “No. elected president” column |
| Most recently elected (year or “never”) | Temporal (year) / categorical for “never” | Text in the “Most recently elected” column |
| Highest previous position (table rows) | Categorical/nominal | Row labels in bottom table |

Overall, this graph provides commentary on the difference in qualifications between our current president and previous presidents.

## 1) Chart type
- **Top panel:** A **categorical timeline dot plot** (scatter/dot plot arranged by category), showing presidents’ first election year against their highest previous position.
- **Bottom panel:** A **table with pictorial marks** (candidate headshots) plus numeric/text columns.

## 2) Layout techniques
- The visualization uses **two vertically stacked panels**.
- **Top panel:** Categories are arranged as horizontal rows; dots are positioned along a shared time axis. This is a **small-multiple-by-row / categorical layout**, not stacked.
- **Bottom panel:** A **tabular layout** with rows for position categories and columns for candidate icons, counts, and most recent election year.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Highest previous position of each U.S. president | Categorical/nominal | Position on y-axis / row placement in top panel |
| Date/year of first election | Temporal | Position on x-axis in top panel |
| Individual president identity (for selected labeled points) | Categorical/nominal | Text labels next to highlighted dots |
| President occurrence / one president per mark | Categorical/nominal (entity) | Individual dot marks in top panel |
| 2020 candidates | Categorical/nominal | Headshot images/icons in the “2020 candidates” column of the table |
| Number elected president | Quantitative | Numeric text in the “No. elected president” column |
| Most recently elected (year or “never”) | Temporal (year) / categorical for “never” | Text in the “Most recently elected” column |
| Highest previous position (table rows) | Categorical/nominal | Row labels in bottom table |

raw_comment: This graph shows the previous government experience (if any) by US presidents, excluding those who assumed the presidency as displayed by the title and the asterisk at the bottom. I notice that most presidents on the graph have had previous government experience and the trend seems to be that if they did hold office in a government position, the timeframe between their service as one and as president is not too spread out, as demonstrated by the yellow dots on the graph and the labeling of the years served as an official and president at the top and on the right side. Voters are more likely to support a candidate who has had previous experience in the field of government and politics. In addition to experience, the familiarity and quality of one's performance also plays a role. This would explain why most of the presidents, except for Eisenhower and Trump, served as president not long after serving in another government position. I wonder how much of a role one's experience in the government plays in a candidate's election? If presidents like Donald Trump can be elected despite government experience, could there be other factors that come into play? ## 1) Chart type

## 2) Layout techniques
- The visualization uses **two vertically stacked panels**.
- **Top panel:** Categories are arranged as horizontal rows; dots are positioned along a shared time axis. This is a **small-multiple-by-row / categorical layout**, not stacked.
- **Bottom panel:** A **tabular layout** with rows for position categories and columns for candidate icons, counts, and most recent election year.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Highest previous position of each U.S. president | Categorical/nominal | Position on y-axis / row placement in top panel |
| Date/year of first election | Temporal | Position on x-axis in top panel |
| Individual president identity (for selected labeled points) | Categorical/nominal | Text labels next to highlighted dots |
| President occurrence / one president per mark | Categorical/nominal (entity) | Individual dot marks in top panel |
| 2020 candidates | Categorical/nominal | Headshot images/icons in the “2020 candidates” column of the table |
| Number elected president | Quantitative | Numeric text in the “No. elected president” column |
| Most recently elected (year or “never”) | Temporal (year) / categorical for “never” | Text in the “Most recently elected” column |
| Highest previous position (table rows) | Categorical/nominal | Row labels in bottom table |
